subject: art-design
title: 3D & Mixed Media: Application
welcome_lead: Mix found objects, transparent layers and unexpected materials into one piece.
meta_desc: GCSE mixed media application: assemblage, layering, found objects, transparent vs opaque.
final_note: Mixing materials lets you push meaning as well as surface.

walkthroughs.body_html: Picasso's bull's head used a bike saddle and handlebars. Assemblage reuses objects, keeping some of their original meaning. Group items by colour, texture or theme first, then test arrangements before fixing them with wire, glue or stitching.

Transparent media like watercolour, ink and tissue paper let earlier marks show through. Opaque media like acrylic and gouache cover what is beneath. Alternating both creates depth — start transparent for atmosphere and finish with opaque for emphasis.

Consider weight: heavy items go low, delicate items high. Mixed media surfaces can include collage, stitch, print and paint together. Always test glue or fixative on a sample first — some solvents dissolve plastics or fade inks.
